brief: A tool caddy with a carry handle and divided bins for screws and bits.

requirements.evidence: Linear 3-cell build (piece:-1,0,0;full, piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) with joint bolts and end caps forms a rigid trough caddy.
Two hex-acc-handle accessories on central cell (accessory:0#0,0#1 and accessory:0#0,0#4 on opposite slots) provide hand clearance to lift/carry the loaded assembly.

requirements.requirement: Divided bins for screws and bits
requirements.evidence: bins: hex-bin-full-div2 at -1,0,0 (2 compartments), hex-bin-full-div2 at 0,0,0 (2 compartments), hex-bin-full-div3 at 1,0,0 (3 compartments) = 7 compartments; dressed with heap-screws-div3 and heap-nuts-div3 in compartments demonstrating screws/bits sorting.

finish.summary: Built 3-cell linear caddy with 2+2+3 divided compartments (7 total) for screws/bits and paired side grab handles on the center cell for carrying. Verified mesh clear; props visible from above.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

parts.name: Grab handle
parts.use: A bar standing off the flat with room for a hand behind it, for a cell or a column that gets moved by its side rather than its top.

parts.name: Trinity handle
parts.use: Reaches across a whole triangle of studs, so a lift is shared between recesses instead of hanging off one, and the cell can be carried loaded.
